The patient is a 10-year-old male with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, and history of warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia who returns for follow-up. His mother reports that he had been fully toilet trained but has recently started to have episodes of fecal incontinence, particularly after school.
outpatient visit, Endocrinology, Dr. Michael Thompson
Two-month history of bedwetting with excessive thirst and frequent urination

The patient presents to the Endocrinology clinic one year following his prior evaluation for functional constipation with enuresis, now with a two-month history of recurrent bedwetting, excessive thirst, and frequent urination. His mother reports that he has been toilet trained since age 3 years with no bedwetting for 4 years until recently.
icu visit, Emergency Medicine, Dr. Emily Watson
Progressive fatigue, weight loss, and increased urination with altered mental status

The patient is an 11-year-old male with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosed six months prior, Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, and a history of warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia, who returns with acute worsening of hyperglycemic symptoms. His mother reports that he has been drinking water constantly, even waking up multiple times during the night to obtain drinks or use the bathroom.

The patient with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, and history of warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia is brought to the emergency department with 2 days of abdominal cramping, fever, and diarrhea. His parents report the diarrhea began watery but has since become bloody.
ed visit, Emergency Medicine, Dr. Aisha Johnson
Profuse watery diarrhea and poor oral intake with decreased urine output

15-year-old male with Type 1 Diabetes and prior Salmonella gastroenteritis is brought to the emergency department after three days of profuse watery diarrhea and poor oral intake during a community outbreak of gastroenteritis. His mother reports markedly decreased urine output and progressive fatigue.
